rules.when: a small or surgical change in a known place, a one-file fix, a rename, a config edit, or a quick factual question about how something works
rules.why: bounded and quick; the cheap fast lane is enough and a strong model at high effort buys nothing here

rules.when: ordinary investigation, code reading, reviewing someone else's proposal, or analysis that needs real understanding but not a structural decision
rules.why: reads and reasons rather than writing code; medium effort is the honest middle

rules.when: difficult, broad, or high-impact architecture: a system boundary, a data model, a migration shape, an ambiguous design with long-term consequences
rules.why: INTERIM LANE. The intended lane is Pi with anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 at xhigh, which is blocked: Pi has no anthropic credential on this machine, so Fable is unreachable from Pi (the model itself runs fine at xhigh under omp). This is the strongest verified Pi lane and holds the architecture slot until Pi gets an anthropic credential, at which point the model here becomes anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 with effort unchanged at xhigh.

rules.when: adversarial review, tenth-man challenge of a plan or a completion claim, or risk analysis before an expensive commitment
rules.why: independent scrutiny, deliberately on Pi and away from the implementation session. Independence is the point: when the work under review was itself produced on gpt-6-astra, override to another strong model such as openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol so the reviewer is not the author

rules.when: ordinary substantial implementation: a bounded feature, normal debugging, a normal refactor, or writing and repairing tests, with a blast radius you can hold in your head
the same kind of implementation work when it spans several files or the design is not fully settled at intake
rules.why: same lane, more thinking; choose between medium and high on actual complexity, not on how the request is phrased

rules.when: hard or large implementation: broad blast radius, cross-stack work, security-sensitive, migration-sensitive, data-integrity-sensitive or concurrency-sensitive changes, difficult production bugs, high-risk refactors
rules.why: two peer lanes, both at xhigh, never downgraded. Choose semantically per task: Opus for long-context work across an unfamiliar repository, subtle invariants, and careful migrations; Astra for dense algorithmic or protocol work and long autonomous tool loops. Weigh task shape, blast radius, reasoning needs, repository context and current provider headroom. Do not reach for Astra merely because a task is difficult, and do not make either the universal default
